sentences.text: applicant is in jail since 26.03.2023.
The bail application of the applicant was rejected by the learned trial court on 16.05.2023.

The following arguments made by Shri Manoj Kumar Tripathi, learned counsel on behalf of the applicant, which could not be satisfactorily refuted by Shri Chandan Agrawal, learned AGA from the record, entitle the applicant for grant of bail:
1. Learned counsel for the applicant contests the minority of the victim as depicted in the prosecution case.
2. The victim was wrongly shown as a minor of 17 years of age in the F.I.R. only to falsely implicate the applicant under the stringent provisions of the POCSO Act and cause his imprisonment.
3.

Learned counsel for the applicant contests the age of the victim set out in the prosecution case in light of the judgement of this Court in Monish Vs. State of U.P.
and others (Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 55026 of 2021) on the following grounds:
(i) There are material contradictions in the age of the victim as recorded in various prosecution documents.
(ii) The age of the victim was incorrectly got registered in the school records by the victim's parents to give her an advantage in life.

entities.text:
Monish Vs. State of U.P.
and others (Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 55026 of 2021)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The school certificate showing her age as 16 years and 4 months is not reliable.
(iii) The victim in her statements under Section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. has asserted that she is 16 years and 6 months of age.
(iv) Medico-legal examination (not the age determination test) records that the victim is 18 to 19 years of age.

(v) No medical examination to determine the correct age of the victim as per the latest scientific criteria and medical protocol by eminent doctors from a reputed institution was got done by the prosecution as it would establish the majority of the victim and falsify the prosecution case.
The victim is in fact a major.
4. The prosecution case set out in the FIR does not make any allegation of abduction or commission of rape by the victim against the applicant.
5. To the contrary the FIR records that the victim was regularly escaping from her house from time to time.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The victim in her statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C. has stated that she left her house of her own volition and thereafter accompanied one Komal to the house of the latter.
The said Komal got her into physical relations with some people.
The victim has also stated that she sent her to the applicant's house where she stayed for a period of one month.

7. The statement of the victim under Section 164 Cr.P.C. contradict her versions as disclosed in her statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C.
8.
The victim has nominated one Nitin Pal as the person who had escorted her to his aunt's place.
She has also asserted that one Chhotu committed rape with her.
9. False and aggravated allegations have been made against the applicant only to save the failing prosecution case and to deflect attention from her own conduct.
10. Major inconsistencies in the FIR, the statement under Section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. discredit the prosecution case.
11. The victim was never confined or bound down in any manner.
The victim was present at various public places but never raised an alarm nor did she resist the applicant.
The conduct of the victim shows that she was a consenting party.
12. Medical evidence to corroborate commission of rape by the applicant with the victim has not been produced by the prosecution.
13. The applicant does not have any criminal history apart from this case.
14. The applicant is not a flight risk.
The applicant being a law abiding citizen has always cooperated with the investigation and undertakes to join the trial proceedings.
There is no possibility of his influencing witnesses, tampering with the evidence or reoffending.
In the light of the preceding discussion and without making any observations on the merits of the case, the bail application is allowed.
Let the applicant-Gufran @ Bhura be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number, on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court below.

The following conditions be imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence or influence any witness during the trial.
(ii) The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.
